01THE THESIS

A skill is a procedure.
A schema is a promise.

Voyager turns successful Minecraft behavior into reusable, executable skills. That is powerful, but a skill alone can be brittle: it knows what to replay, not which assumptions made it safe.

SchemaVoyager adds an explicit world model. Every recipe or mining mechanic carries preconditions, predicted effects, and evidence from a verified episode. The agent can plan with those promises, then roll them back when reality disagrees.

02THE LOOP

From observation
to reusable behavior.

Click through one episode. The agent does not just remember a transcript; it promotes a successful interaction into a compact object it can replay and check.

CURRENT STATE

See what the world gives you.

The environment emits a compact observation: position, nearby blocks, inventory, action budget, and the goal. The agent starts with facts, not a long replay.

observation = {
  goal: "wooden_pickaxe",
  inventory: {},
  visible_blocks: {"log": 2}
}
03ARCHITECTURE

One agent.
Two memories.

The environment stays replaceable. The learned state stays inspectable. That separation lets the same loop run against the deterministic starter world today and MineDojo or Mineflayer tomorrow.

→

04THE MEMORY FORMAT

Rules make skills
accountable.

Both objects are plain data. That makes the agent's improvement visible in a code review, replayable in a test, and easy to replace with an LLM-backed induction step.

A / WORLD RULECERTIFIED

craft:wooden_pickaxe

"preconditions": [
  "inventory[planks] >= 3",
  "inventory[sticks] >= 2"
],
"predicted_effects": [
  "inventory[wooden_pickaxe] += 1"
],
"evidence": ["t1_wooden_pickaxe"]
confidence02 / 05
B / EXECUTABLE SKILLREPLAYABLE

skill_wooden_pickaxe

"steps": [
  "move",
  "mine",
  "craft"
],
"postconditions": [
  "inventory[wooden_pickaxe] >= 1"
],
"validator": "replay + check"
version01 / 01
05THE CURRICULUM

Small world.
Real transfer.

Three training episodes teach the progression. Three holdouts move the spawn, stretch the distance, or hand over a partial inventory. The goal is to prove reuse before adding complexity.

IDMISSIONWHAT CHANGESSTATUS
T1wooden pickaxetwo nearby logsTRAIN
T2stone pickaxewooden pickaxe + sticksTRAIN
T3furnaceeight stone blocksTRAIN
H1wooden pickaxenew spawn coordinatesHOLDOUT
H2stone pickaxedistant stone + partial kitHOLDOUT
H3furnacewide field + new spawnHOLDOUT
